scenes.title: Where to find an OKX referral code

media.image_prompt: a person looking at a smartphone with curiosity in a bright apartment, morning light, soft focus background

lines.show: A valid OKX referral code comes from someone who already has an OKX account: a friend, a creator, or your own app.
And you can test it in seconds, inside the sign-up screen.
Let's go through where codes come from, how to find your own, and how to check one.
There are three normal sources.
First, a friend or family member who already uses OKX can share their code with you.
Second, creators often share their code in a video or a pinned comment.
Third, once you have an account, your own code sits in the app's invite section.

scenes.title: A code is just letters
scenes.text: No file, no download, no payment.

lines.show: Remember what a code is: a short string of letters or numbers.
It never comes as a file to install, and you never pay anyone to get one.

scenes.title: Skip codes sold or traded
scenes.text: A real code is shared, not sold.

lines.show: If someone asks for money, a deposit, or your login in exchange for a code, walk away.
Referral codes are shared freely by people who already use the platform.

scenes.title: Find your code in the app

lines.show: Already have an account and want your own code? Here's where to look.
Open the OKX app and log in.
Open the main menu or your profile.
Look for a section called Invite friends or Referral. Names can change between app versions.
There you'll see your code, ready to copy and share.

scenes.title: Share it the clean way
scenes.text: Code only. Let people type it themselves.

lines.show: When you share your code, share just the code.
Let the other person type it into the official app themselves. That keeps everyone safe.
The easiest check is the sign-up screen itself.
When you type a code in the referral field, the app usually flags a code that doesn't exist.
If it's accepted, the code is valid for registration.

scenes.title: Code rejected? Check these
scenes.text: Spaces, zeros and the letter O.

lines.show: If the app rejects a code, don't give up on it right away.
Delete any space before or after it, and check that a zero wasn't typed instead of the letter O.
Still rejected? Ask the person who shared it to send it again.

scenes.title: Code accepted, now what?
scenes.text: Read the rewards page before anything else.

lines.show: So the code went through. What should you do next?
Open the rewards page in the app and read what applies to you, including tasks and deadlines.
Then turn on two-factor authentication before you do anything else.

scenes.title: A code you can use
scenes.text: Type it in the referral field

lines.show: If you don't have a code yet, you can use this one: XOACPQFC.
Type it letter by letter in the referral field during sign-up.

scenes.title: If OKX is available where you live

lines.show: If OKX is available where you live, enter code XOACPQFC when you create your account.
The sign-up link is in the description.
Check the rewards page first, and thanks for watching.
